edition.alertText: IRGC launches drones at Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait — targets Patriot air defenses; Kuwait condemns 'dangerous escalation', invokes UNSCR 2817 and Article 51; Bahrain air defenses intercept 'several' more Iranian air strikes — attacks now span Bahrain, Kuwait, and strait; IRGC claims 3 tankers caught fire after hitting mines east of Hormuz on Nov 19 — vessels allegedly had navigation systems off; ADNOC L&S vessel attacked transiting Hormuz (Nov 18) — 1 crew member missing, 11 injured; Saudi Arabia, UAE, GCC condemn attacks on Kuwait, Bahrain, and ADNOC tanker; Trump arrives in Shenzhen — Xi greets him on tarmac; Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral summit today (Nov 19) at 2:30 PM local — Iran conflict and nuclear arms on agenda; Saudi coalition strikes 60 Houthi targets including underground missile storage; intercepts cruise missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh; Reuters: Saudi Arabia preparing Yemen campaign to last into 2027; Yemen designates Houthis as terrorist organization; DNI Clayton: Iranian threats inside and outside US have 'dramatically increased'; US reissues Gulf security warnings; IAEA Grossi: inspections limited to Bushehr — underground Isfahan enrichment plant uninspected; war-risk insurance per Hormuz transit reaches $64M vs $54K pre-war (US Navy); oil declines — Brent $92.25 (-0.96%), WTI $84.55 (-1.70%); API: US crude stocks +5.28M bbl; IEA: global supply up 2.3M b/d in Oct to 105.4M b/d, sees Q4 surplus; gold drops sharply to ~$3,750; ADNOC sees sulfur output doubling — CEO calls sulfur 'the future gold'; JMIC: 177 maritime security incidents since Mar 1; daily Hormuz transits in single digits vs 138/day pre-war

situation: The conflict expanded to a new front on Wednesday as the IRGC launched drones at Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait, claiming to have targeted US Patriot air defense systems and drone and missile launch platforms — the first confirmed Iranian strikes on Kuwait in months. Kuwait's military confirmed its air defenses were countering hostile drone attacks and that explosions residents heard came from interceptions. Kuwait's Foreign Ministry condemned the attack as a 'dangerous escalation' undermining diplomacy, invoking UN Security Council Resolution 2817 and Article 51 of the UN Charter. Hours later, Bahrain's Defence Force reported intercepting 'several' Iranian air strikes — continuing a week-long pattern of attacks on the Gulf state. Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and GCC Secretary-General Albudaiwi condemned the attacks on Kuwait, Bahrain, and an ADNOC tanker, with the GCC calling on the UN Security Council to act. Trump arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday evening, with Xi Jinping greeting him on the tarmac in a rare gesture — the first time in approximately 50 years a Chinese leader has met a visiting dignitary at the airport. The Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral summit is scheduled for 2:30 PM local time today (November 19), with Iran and nuclear arms control as key agenda items. Sources close to mediators described Iran as 'not showing any flexibility,' with the US 'listening but not responding.' Tehran continued to insist the US must lift its blockade before Iran halts Hormuz attacks. DNI Clayton told Congress that Iranian threats inside and outside the US have 'dramatically increased.' The IAEA's Grossi confirmed inspections have been limited to Bushehr, with the underground Isfahan enrichment plant remaining uninspected. Yemen designated the Houthi group as a terrorist organization, with FM Al-Zouba urging partners to follow suit.

Oil prices continued their decline on Wednesday, with Brent crude falling to $92.25/bbl (-0.96%) and WTI sliding to $84.55/bbl (-1.70%), pressured by an API report showing US crude stocks rose 5.28 million barrels in the week ending November 13 — the second consecutive large inventory build — alongside gasoline stocks up 5.12 million barrels and distillates up 351,000 barrels. The IEA's November report confirmed global supply rose 2.3 million b/d in October to 105.4 million b/d, with global inventories up 52 million barrels, reinforcing the Q4 surplus narrative. Brent is now down approximately 21% from its October peak above $116. Gold dropped sharply to approximately $3,750/oz, extending its decline well below the $3,904 level seen earlier this week, as expectations of a December Fed rate hike (CME FedWatch odds near 85%) continued to crush precious metals. Coal held steady at approximately $145/tonne, supported by Middle East tensions and high LNG prices heading into winter. War-risk insurance for a single Hormuz transit has surged to $64 million per tanker, up from approximately $54,000 pre-war, according to the US Navy chief's testimony to the Senate. ADNOC's sour gas CEO Al Jaberi described sulfur as 'the future gold' at the Middle East Gas Conference in Dubai, as ADNOC plans to double sulfur output from 7 million tonnes to 14-20 million tonnes by 2030-2035. Sulfur spot prices have eased from June-July peaks of $1,100-1,300/tonne to $740-890/tonne by mid-October (Kpler), though still well above the pre-war average of ~$500/tonne (CRU). The IAEA-US-Saudi nuclear agreement was described as 'very satisfactory' by Grossi, though Trump conditioned further progress on Saudi joining the Abraham Accords.

An ADNOC Logistics & Services vessel was attacked on Tuesday evening while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, leaving one crew member missing and eleven injured. ADNOC confirmed this was part of what it has described as over 15 'unprovoked' attacks on its vessels since the war began, calling the strikes 'piracy.' Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and the Arab Interior Ministers Council condemned the ADNOC attack. On Wednesday morning, Iran's IRIB reported that three oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines east of the Strait of Hormuz — the IRGC claimed the vessels had their navigation systems switched off and were operating in restricted areas without Iranian coordination, warning ships against using 'fake American routes.' At least five vessels were reported hit in the area in recent days. The Saudi-led coalition struck 60 Houthi military targets on Tuesday, including underground ballistic missile storage facilities across four Yemeni cities. The Houthi-run health ministry said at least 17 people were killed, including 15 at a sponge factory in Hodeidah. The coalition intercepted cruise missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh, with civil defense alerts issued for Najran, Jazan, Khamis Mushait, and Sharurah. Reuters reported that Saudi Arabia is preparing for its Yemen campaign to last into 2027, with the campaign expected to run six more months. JMIC's cumulative count has risen to 177 maritime security incidents since March 1, with daily Hormuz transits remaining in the single digits compared with approximately 138 per day pre-war. About 162 ships remain anchored near Fujairah and Khor Fakkan. The US State Department reissued security warnings for Americans in Saudi Arabia and Bahrain.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices eased from June-July peaks of $1,100-1,300/tonne to $740-890/tonne by mid-October (Kpler), but remain above pre-war avg of ~$500/tonne (CRU). ADNOC sees sulfur output doubling from 7M to 14-20M tonnes by 2030-2035 — CEO Al Jaberi calls sulfur 'the future gold' (Nov 18). ADNOC's Oct official selling price cut $70 to $890/tonne. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%; DAP at $803/mt in October, ~30% above January (IFDC). Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst). China phosphate exports near zero in 2026, down from ~5.3M mt in 2025 (IFDC).

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for fourth consecutive month — September, October, and early November all zero (World Visualized/Syz Group/Fertilizer Daily). UN official Jorge Moreira da Silva at COP31 (Nov 14) warns 45 million people could face severe food insecurity — urges US and Iran to immediately allow ~5 fertilizer vessels/day through Hormuz within 7-10 days. Fertilizer prices up ~30% since blockades began (UN). Sudan food prices doubled in 6 months; Nepal farmers cannot afford fertiliser. Countries facing significant impact: Mozambique, Kenya, Sudan, Somalia, Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka. Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). DAP at $803/mt in October, urea near January levels after April spike (IFDC Bulletin #37). Egypt gas supply cuts to fertilizer producers rose from 20% to 33% on Nov 8 — AGF Nitrogen running at 80-85% capacity (IFDC). Russia export quotas Dec 2026–May 2027 at ~18.8M mt, down from ~20M mt. IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement. Middle East fertiliser exports declined by 70% as Iran war disrupts supplies (The National).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Qatar LNG loadings pick up to roughly half of pre-war levels (Bloomberg, Nov 10). Global LNG supply gap estimated at ~600 bcf. Dutch TTF gas eased to ~€89.59/MWh (~$100.85), down from 4-year high above €101/MWh prior week; EU gas storage at 74.33% full vs 86% five-year average — lowest in over a decade entering winter (IEA). LNG crossings at Hormuz reached 32 in October — highest since war began (S&P Global). IRGC claims gas carrier exploded after mine strike in eastern Hormuz (Nov 13). Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Bangladesh struggling with spot market costs. Lufthansa says 2026 fuel costs €2B higher amid Iran war. Europe and Asia face tight supply heading into winter. JERA CEO says Qatar LNG supply unlikely to recover soon. EIA projects US heating oil households to pay $2,977 this winter — up 70.2% from last year. IMF projects 2026 GDP contractions: Kuwait and Iraq ~16%, Qatar ~15%. LNG flows at 40-45% of prewar levels (Daniel Davis estimate, Nov 18).
